title: Earl King and Jesse Allen stand in for Slim and Ray Charles
summary: After Slim hit a bulldozer, Earl King played Slim and Jesse Allen played Ray Charles in Alabama and Atlanta.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Did you collect records? Collect records at all? No.
Photograph records? I can tell you an incident about when he ran into the bulldozer on La Salle Street.
Yeah, tell me that one because I think I heard that one. I heard a version of that one. You heard a version of that one?

A version of that one. I'll hear your version. Okay, well, I don't know what happened but he was drunk or probably was high or something. He ran into a bulldozer. Right in the square where La Salle runs into the ferret. Ferret runs to La Salle wherever that point is down there. There's a bulldozer sitting up there and Slim, he ran into it with his car. And he had to end up going to Charity Hospital. We had some dates we had to perform and Jose said, we need, Cotton, what are we going to do? Slim got to go play in Bessma, Alabama. What are we going to do? I said, there's a guy right upstairs that played and looked almost like Slim. Earl King. He told you that story?
Yeah, but I want to hear your version.

So I told Jose, I said, yeah, man, I said, Earl, Earl can do this for you. He said, yes? I said, yeah. So I went up there and went knocked on his door. I said, man, look, Jose want to see you. He said, we might have a gig for you. You know all Slim's tunes. Yeah, Cotton, I know him. He came on down. We met Jose and Jose said, yeah, well, we're going to go to Bessma, Alabama. So then we said, well, Ray Charles is supposed to come. I said, but Ray Charles in California, he won't be able to make that date. So we took Jesse, what was his last name?

Took Jesse Allen to go as Ray Charles. Earl King to go as Guitar Slim. Now, we had played in Flint, Michigan. We had played up there with the regular band with Slim before this happened. They had some people up there. We talked with them and everything went down fine. Now, we went to Bessma, Alabama with Earl as Slim and Jesse as Ray Charles. Now, Jesse put his glasses on but he's going to go stand by the mic and sing. I'm sitting at the piano playing. So we had uniforms on. We came out with a, we had a rust uniform. We came out with the rust uniforms. We played the first part for Guitar Slim. Then we took intermission, we went back in, we put our green uniforms on to come back and play with Jesse Allen. And Jesse knew all the Ray Charles songs, man. And they had a guy out there in the audience. He looked up there and he kept looking. He said, man, damn old Guitar Slim. Damn Guitar Slim. So I told Gus, Gus was the announcer for us. Gus Farton F No. Gus did all announcing the tall guy at the alto. I said, Gus, call Jose back there. So we stopped and before we played the next number he called Jose to come to the stage. And Jose came back and we punished the guy out downstairs. So Jose brought the guy inside and we butted him up and talked to him. Otherwise we was going to get our butts kicked. No telling what would have happened. Well the promoter didn't know what was going on? Well I think Jose talked with him. Oh, he talked to him. He talked to him. He said, look, we got somebody we know we can do this. A lot of people used to do this. Because when we went to California, as far as we know, Guitar Slam had been there. Then people said, no, Slam been here. The guy said, look, I'm Guitar Slam. Now whoever you had before, he was not the real person. So that happens. But Jose and the manager, whoever the producer was in Bessman, Alabama, when they got it together. Then we left there and we went to Atlanta. The same thing. But after that, then we, but Ray Charles met us in Atlanta. And Jesse Allen came on back home. But Earl, I think he went to Atlanta too with us if I remember right. I think he told me he did. Yeah. Yeah. But other than that, that's all I can remember. But if it had been for Earl, we would not have made those two engagements. Those two dates. Those two dates, yeah.
Yeah, I think you played in Atlanta for Mr. Beeman. Yes. Mr. Beeman. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah.

I have been to Atlanta. I don't know. I don't even know what it looked like. They've revamped everything and everything is, it's all together different around there. Just like the Dewdrop is not the same anymore. In fact, even the 5-4 Bar Room in Los Angeles is not the same. The one in Detroit, they had a Wala Haja Hotel we played in Atlanta. That's not there anymore. We played a hotel in Detroit. That's not there anymore. So all the places that we plant, they're no longer in existence, you know?
Yeah. That's life. That's how things change. Yeah. That's how things change. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah.
